stem: Glasgow Analytics runs an EC2 fleet in private subnets that calls Amazon S3 constantly, and that traffic is the largest line item passing through the fleet's NAT gateway on the monthly bill.

choices.text: Enable Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration for the fleet's S3 requests
Create a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC
Front the S3 traffic with AWS Global Accelerator
Move the EC2 fleet into the same Availability Zone as its egress path

rationale: A gateway endpoint for S3 removes that traffic from the NAT gateway's data path entirely, at no additional charge. S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds long-distance uploads over the internet, it does not apply to private-subnet traffic routed through a NAT gateway. Global Accelerator improves routing performance for TCP/UDP endpoints, it does not remove NAT processing charges. Moving the fleet to the same Availability Zone as its egress path can reduce cross-Availability-Zone charges but leaves the underlying per-gigabyte NAT charge for S3 traffic untouched.
